metaDescription: Five iPhone stands compared by sturdiness, adjustability and fold size, from a 2.2 oz foldable to a charging-cutout aluminum stand for heavy cases.
introParagraphs: An iPhone stand turns the phone into a small hands-free screen for video calls, recipes, photos and bedside clocks, which is why a good one is useful far beyond the desk. This roundup compares five stands that all work with iPhones, ranging from the UGREEN at 2.2 oz that folds to 3.74 by 3.35 inches to the OMOTON C2 with a 3 mm aluminum base and a charging cutout.

The spread comes down to three things: how stable the stand is, how adjustable the angle is, and how small it folds. The UGREEN adjusts from 0 to 100 degrees with an automatic lock, the OGMAPLE folds to 4.33 by 2.6 by 1.06 inches, and the Lamicall supports phones from 4 to 8 inches. The Nulaxy comes as a two-pack, which suits a home with a stand at the desk and another in the kitchen.

We evaluated each stand based on product specs and buyer feedback, with attention to how well it holds a phone in a case and how easy it is to adjust with one hand. The ranking favors stands that stay put, set up in seconds and do not require fiddly knobs.

products.name: UGREEN Foldable Phone Stand
products.description:
The UGREEN balances portability and sturdiness better than the other picks. It weighs just 2.2 oz and folds to 3.74 by 3.35 inches, yet its triangle structure is described as stable even for larger phones. An automatic lock mechanism holds the angle anywhere from 0 to 100 degrees without a knob to tighten.

The tradeoff is that a lightweight folding stand is still lighter than a weighted base, so a heavy phone in a thick case can tip if tapped hard. Because the hinge locks automatically, you adjust it with one hand and no tools. That is a real advantage over designs that rely on friction joints that loosen.

In ownership, the stand needs only an occasional wipe, and the folded size slips into a pocket or drawer. It is listed near the low end of the cost range, second cheapest of the candidates. Compared with the OMOTON C2, it is lighter and more portable, while the OMOTON gives you a heavier base for the same money class.
products.bestFor: Everyday desk and travel use with one-hand adjustment
pros: Light at 2.2 oz and folds small
cons: May tip under hard taps with heavy cases

products.name: OMOTON C2 Aluminum Phone Stand
products.description:
The OMOTON C2 is a fixed-style stand with a thicker 3mm aluminum body and a larger 4.1 by 3 by 4.4 inch footprint. The listing highlights a hook long enough to hold phones with heavy cases still on, plus a non-slip silicone surface. A charging cutout lets you leave a cable plugged in during a video call.

The tradeoff is bulk. It does not fold flat like the UGREEN or Nulaxy, so it lives on a desk instead of in a pocket. The 270-degree rotation lets you change the viewing angle freely, though without a locking hinge you rely on friction.

Because it is thicker and wider, it is the steadiest stand in the lineup, and a stable base matters for FaceTime and taps. It costs a little more than the UGREEN and a lot less than the Nulaxy pack. Choose it if the phone wears a rugged case or the stand will be a permanent desk fixture.
products.bestFor: Heavy cases and permanent desk or kitchen use
pros: Hook fits phones with heavy cases
Charging cutout keeps the cable connected
cons: Does not fold flat for travel
Friction hinge has no locking mechanism

products.name: Lamicall Aluminum Phone Stand
products.description:
The Lamicall is a clean aluminum alloy stand with a smooth finish and a stated range of 4 to 8 inch phones, which covers every current iPhone and small tablets. It offers adjustable viewing angles for calls, movies and reading. The metal build gives it more heft than plastic stands.

The tradeoff is that the listing says little about a locking hinge, so check the angle holds under taps. Because the stand is a classic desktop design, it does not fold as small as the UGREEN or OGMAPLE.

Day to day it needs only a wipe, and the smooth edges mean it will not scratch a bag or desk. It sits in the mid-range of cost. Against the OMOTON C2, it has a wider stated device range but lacks the charging cutout and the heavy-case hook.
products.bestFor: A tidy metal desk stand for phones and small tablets
cons: Does not fold as small as the UGREEN

products.name: Nulaxy Dual Folding Phone Stands, 2-Pack
products.description:
The Nulaxy set gives you two aluminum stands with height and angle adjustment, so one can stay at the desk and the other in a bag or kitchen. The dual folding design lets you raise the phone closer to eye level, which helps with video calls. It collapses fully when you are done.

The tradeoff is that the dual hinge adds moving parts, which means more places for the joint to loosen over time. The set is also the premium pick by cost, because you are buying two stands.

For couples or a home with two rooms, the pair is cheaper per stand than two separate premium models. Compared with the UGREEN, it adds height adjustment, but the UGREEN is lighter at 2.2 oz and cheaper. Choose the Nulaxy when you want eye-level height and a spare.
products.bestFor: Homes that want one stand at the desk and a spare elsewhere
pros: Two aluminum stands in one purchase
Raises the phone toward eye level
cons: Dual hinges give more joints to loosen

products.name: OGMAPLE Mini Folding Phone Stand
products.description:
The OGMAPLE is the smallest and lowest-cost stand here, folding to 4.33 by 2.6 by 1.06 inches. A silicone pad on the panel protects the phone from scratches, and the base has grip features to keep it from sliding. It is compatible with 5 to 8 inch devices.

The tradeoff is stability. A very compact stand has a shorter base, so it suits phones in light cases better than heavy ones. It also offers fewer adjustment steps than the UGREEN.

For a spare in a purse or a gift stocking, it is hard to beat at this cost. Compared with the UGREEN, it saves a little money but offers less locking angle control. Choose it when portability and price matter more than perfect steadiness.
products.bestFor: A pocket-size spare stand at the lowest cost
pros: Folds to a tiny 1.06 inch thickness
cons: Short base is less stable with heavy cases
Fewer angle options than the UGREEN

buyingCriteria.explanation: A stand that tips during a tap or a FaceTime call is the most common complaint. The OMOTON C2 uses a 3mm aluminum body at 4.1 by 3 by 4.4 inches, while the OGMAPLE folds to just 1.06 inches thick. Heavier, wider bases resist tipping, and plastic stands tend to wobble compared with aluminum. Choose the OMOTON for a permanent spot and the UGREEN's triangle structure for portable use.

Check the stated device range and whether the stand handles a case. The Lamicall lists 4 to 8 inch phones and the OGMAPLE 5 to 8 inch devices, and the OMOTON's hook is meant for heavy cases. A universal fit claim is marketing, so measure your phone plus case. If you use a rugged case, favor the OMOTON over a thin foldable.

The UGREEN adjusts from 0 to 100 degrees with an automatic lock, while the OMOTON offers 270 degrees of rotation on a friction joint. A locking hinge is easier on tired hands because you do not need to tighten a knob. For seniors, favor large, simple adjustments with few steps. A good rule is to pick the lock style first and the angle range second.

The UGREEN weighs 2.2 oz and folds to 3.74 by 3.35 inches, while the OGMAPLE folds to 4.33 by 2.6 by 1.06 inches. Foldable models carry easily but are usually less stable than fixed ones. If the stand mostly stays at home, size matters less than stability. If you travel often, the UGREEN at 2.2 oz is the easiest of these to carry.

A charging cutout lets you keep the cable plugged in during a long call. The OMOTON C2 includes one, and open-design stands can also leave the port clear. Check the cutout position against your phone's port, especially if you use a thick case. Always check where the cable exits your phone before trusting a cutout.

Silicone or rubber padding protects the phone and the desk from scratches. The OGMAPLE has a silicone pad on the panel and the OMOTON uses non-slip silicone. Cheap bare-metal stands can scratch the phone, so confirm the contact points are padded. A quick wipe with a damp cloth keeps the pads grippy and the finish clean.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared base size and material, from the OMOTON's 3mm aluminum body to the OGMAPLE's compact fold. Heavier and wider bases scored higher. We also weighed buyer feedback about tipping.

howWeEvaluated.title: Adjustability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at angle range and locking, such as the UGREEN's 0 to 100 degrees with an auto lock and the Nulaxy's height and angle control. Easier one-hand adjustment scored higher. Friction-only joints scored lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared folded sizes and weights, including the UGREEN at 2.2 oz and the OGMAPLE at 1.06 inches thick. This criterion carried less weight for desk-only users. It matters for travel.

howWeEvaluated.title: Device and case fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked the stated device range, such as the Lamicall at 4 to 8 inches, and heavy-case provisions like the OMOTON hook. The strongest pick, the UGREEN, was set against the most basic, the OGMAPLE, for fit and stability. Fit and stability together decided most of the ranking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared cost tiers against features, noting the OGMAPLE as the lowest cost and the Nulaxy two-pack as the premium. We favored stands where each added feature justified the cost. Features that did not change daily use earned little credit.

cards.label: Folding (UGREEN, OGMAPLE, Nulaxy)
cards.text: These collapse to fit a pocket or bag and suit travel. They are lighter, so they can tip with heavy phones. The UGREEN is the steadiest of the folding group.

cards.label: Fixed (OMOTON C2, Lamicall)
cards.text: These stay open and weigh more, which gives them better stability. They take more desk room and are less portable.

howToChoose.note: Recommendation: choose a folding UGREEN for flexibility and a fixed OMOTON C2 for a permanent spot.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Choose a stand with a firm base and a locking or well-gripping angle, because a bouncing screen is tiring to watch. Height adjustment brings the camera closer to eye level.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Nulaxy gives height adjustment and the OMOTON C2 gives the steadiest base. The UGREEN is the best all-round choice if you also travel with it.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more on the OMOTON C2 if your case is heavy or the stand stays on a desk, and on the Nulaxy two-pack if you want height adjustment and a spare.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save with the UGREEN or OGMAPLE if you mostly need portability. The UGREEN is the better steadiness for the money.

faq.q: How do I choose between a folding and a fixed iPhone stand?
faq.a: Think about where the stand will live. A folding stand like the UGREEN or OGMAPLE slips into a pocket or bag and suits travel. A fixed stand like the OMOTON C2 or Lamicall is heavier and steadier for a desk. If you use it mostly at home, stability matters more than fold size.

faq.q: Which iPhone stand works with a thick case?
faq.a: The OMOTON C2 is built for it, with a hook long enough to hold phones with heavy cases on. The Lamicall supports phones from 4 to 8 inches, but you should still measure phone plus case. Avoid very small stands if your case is bulky.

faq.q: Are cheap phone stands worth it?
faq.a: Often yes, for light use. The OGMAPLE is the lowest-cost pick and folds tiny, but it is less stable with heavy phones. If you will use the stand daily, the UGREEN gives better steadiness for a small step up in cost.

faq.q: Will the stand scratch my phone?
faq.a: Look for silicone or rubber padding at the contact points. The OGMAPLE and OMOTON C2 both use silicone, which protects the phone. Bare metal stands can scratch, so check the listing.

faq.q: Can I charge the phone while it is on the stand?
faq.a: Yes, if the stand has a cutout or an open design. The OMOTON C2 has a charging cutout, and open stands like the Lamicall leave the port accessible. Check that your cable and case allow it.

The hinge is the weak point. Locking hinges like the UGREEN's resist loosening better than friction joints, and the Nulaxy has two hinges to monitor. Avoid forcing the stand past its stop to extend its life.

faq.q: Can these stands hold a tablet?
faq.a: Some can hold small tablets. The Lamicall lists up to 8 inches and the OGMAPLE 5 to 8 inch devices, but a full-size iPad is beyond them. For a larger screen, look for a tablet-specific stand.
